name: Tomas Quinn

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI firms, employers, unions or government. We sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers are confidential. What is a normal workday?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I teach beginner bass on Wednesdays, play a Sunday lunch set with a guitarist at the cafe, and record simple tracks for local singers. I finished secondary school and am still learning how to teach a group; one child at a time is easier.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What brings you back, and what wears you down?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I like seeing a child keep time with another child. I dislike the mortgage date coming round when my partner’s care shifts and my cafe dates both change.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the cafe owner that AI making the booking list easier is fine, but customers still ask for a bassist at the Sunday lunch set. I would keep showing up for the paid set.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I am not worried about the booking form, but I am worried about the mortgage. My partner’s care shifts are often cut short, and our savings would not cover a full month.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I will keep the Sunday cafe set and the Wednesday beginner bass pupils this winter. I already use AI sometimes to draft a pupil practice sheet, and I will continue checking the fingering before handing it over.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the household money even in a quiet AI picture. A cancelled Sunday set means the groceries have to come from somewhere else.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What happened at the cafe on the last poor Sunday?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Last month one wet Sunday had half the usual crowd and the owner paid the agreed fee anyway. I would ask for the same written fee next term rather than rely on his kindness.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which family cost would change first?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My son wants new football boots. I would buy used ones first if the winter sets thin out, though I would rather earn enough to get the new pair.

say: I would tell the cafe that **Sunday bass** still draws regular customers.
I would ask for the **agreed live fee** in writing.
think: Our **thin savings** and variable care shifts make the mortgage vulnerable.
A missed **Sunday set** would reach the grocery budget quickly.
do: Keep **Sunday cafe sets** and Wednesday bass lessons this winter.
Ask the owner for a **written fee** for next term’s Sundays.
Buy **used football boots** if winter cafe sets thin out.
feel: I feel **anxious** about household bills even when AI changes little.
S0.quote: A cancelled Sunday set means the groceries have to come from somewhere else.
fieldNote: His **care-worker partner** has variable shifts and the household lacks one month of savings.
The wet-Sunday **written fee** is a concrete protection he wants repeated next term.

steps.text: Keep Sunday cafe bass sets and Wednesday pupils
Buy used football boots if winter cafe sets thin out

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say the cafe might use AI for bookings, posters and background music, and I would ask what happens to the Sunday band fee. I would show the owner how many customers stay through the set.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The little recording tracks I make for local singers could go first. A lost Sunday duo fee would leave lessons carrying the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I would ask the owner for three months of Sunday dates in writing and keep a count of tables during our set. If the cafe reduces dates in the first year, I would ask the school music room about a paid after-school bass group, but only if a teacher can supervise it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be anxious because the cafe might cut paid nights, but the owner has not said he will. Asking for dates gives me something real to work from.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What condition would the school place on a bass group?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The school room is free only while a staff teacher stays. I would not leave children there with me alone because the school requires a staff member present.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you use AI to teach that group?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I use AI now and then for practice sheets, but I would not play a machine track behind pupils without listening through it. One bad beat can teach a beginner the wrong thing.

I would show the owner **table counts** during our live set.
think: My **recording tracks** may lose buyers as AI produces cheap music.

do: Request three months of **cafe dates** in writing this month.
Ask for a paid **school bass group** if cafe dates fall and a teacher supervises.
Keep **Wednesday bass pupils** while the cafe decides its spring dates.
feel: I feel **anxious** about possible lost nights, while the cafe has not cut them yet.
S1.quote: A lost Sunday duo fee would leave lessons carrying the mortgage.
fieldNote: He separates likely **recording income loss** from a cafe decision that remains uncertain and could hit the mortgage.
The school group needs a **staff supervisor**, not merely an available room.

steps.text: Keep Wednesday bass pupils while cafe dates are checked
Start a paid school bass group if cafe dates fall and a teacher supervises

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the cafe that AGI by 2028 may write and book the whole set, but our duo still plays for people at lunch. I would ask the owner for a decision before he changes the fee.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The recording tracks likely go in 2028, and I expect the cafe to try a generated playlist and cut our paid set. Robots for hands-on work come around 2031. The cafe could stop paying musicians before a robot touches a bass.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Tomorrow I would ask the owner whether our next twelve Sundays are booked, and I would ask the school if its supervised group has a paid opening. If the cafe cancels our sets after 2028, I would apply for a nearby music-shop assistant vacancy and call the lender before missing a mortgage payment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be alarmed if the cafe drops us, and I think that could happen quickly. There is no full month of savings to cover a long gap.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Is the music-shop vacancy still real?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The music shop advertised one part-time opening last week, but it might be filled. I would apply only while it is open and keep lessons until another pay cheque starts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell your partner that night?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell my partner that we can keep the children’s lessons for now, but we must watch the mortgage date. I would not pretend the shop job is already mine.

say: I would ask the cafe for a **fee decision** before it changes our Sundays.
I would say our **live duo** still gives lunch customers a reason to stay.
think: My **recording tracks** likely lose buyers in 2028 before 2031 stage robots.
The cafe could cut **live pay** even before a robot plays bass.
do: Ask the cafe about **twelve booked Sundays** tomorrow and keep bass pupils until another pay cheque starts.
Apply for an **open music-shop post** if the cafe cancels sets after 2028.
Call the **mortgage lender** before arrears if the cafe cancels our sets.
feel: I feel **alarmed** at a likely cafe loss with less than a month saved.
S2.quote: The cafe could stop paying musicians before a robot touches a bass.
fieldNote: He identifies **2028 thinking AI** as a risk to recordings and cafe buying choices.
His fallback needs a **real vacancy**; mortgage contact comes before arrears, not after.

steps.text: Apply for an open music-shop job if cafe sets end after 2028
Call the mortgage lender before missing a payment if cafe sets end

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell my children that AGI by 2031 gives us some time to make Sunday work less important to the mortgage. I would ask the school about a proper supervised bass class.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I still expect recording tracks to dry up in 2031. Stage robots around 2034 could take live sets too, though I do not know whether the cafe would choose one.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This term I would ask the school for one paid after-school bass block with a staff teacher in the room. If six children enroll and the school pays for preparation, I would teach it; in the first year after 2031 I would keep the class only while those conditions hold.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be anxious. Five years gives me time to test a class, but our mortgage still depends on weekly work now.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How many pupils make the school block real?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Six pupils would cover the school’s minimum for the block. If only three sign up, I would keep the private lessons and ask again next term.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you use the practice-sheet tool there?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would use the practice-sheet tool I know to draft exercises, then check fingerings on my bass. I would not let the software decide whether a child is ready to play in front of others.

I would tell my children that we can **test new work** before 2031.
think: My **recording tracks** may dry up by 2031 before 2034 stage robots.
The **mortgage** still needs weekly pay while a class is tested.

Keep the **paid school block** after 2031 only while enrollment, supervision and preparation pay continue.
feel: I feel **anxious** because five years does not cover next month’s mortgage.
S3.quote: Five years gives me time to test a class, but our mortgage still depends on weekly work now.
fieldNote: He sets **six pupils** plus staff supervision and preparation pay as conditions for a school group.

steps.text: Teach the school bass block after 2031 if six enroll, staff supervises and preparation is paid
Keep private bass lessons if only three pupils enroll

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the children that AGI by 2036 leaves years to learn an instrument and a way to earn from it. I would still ask the school to pay for any extra class I teach.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If the after-school block lasts, by 2036 I might be less dependent on Sunday cafe sets. Robots around 2039 could play bass at lunch, but I cannot know what the owner will buy.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Starting this year I would save one paid lesson fee in good months after the mortgage and food clear. In the first year after 2036 I would compare actual cafe dates with school and private lesson pay, and apply for an open music-shop job if the cafe income falls and lessons cannot cover the gap.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be anxious, not calm. A ten-year plan does not pay this winter’s mortgage, and my partner’s care shifts can still fall short.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Can you save a lesson fee every month?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Some months there is no spare lesson fee. I would rather skip the savings envelope than borrow for groceries.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell your children about work?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell my children to finish school and learn a skill they can take to different jobs. I do not want them thinking music is the only honest work.

I would insist that any **extra school class** is paid.
think: A lasting **school block** might reduce dependence on Sunday cafe pay.
The **mortgage** and uncertain care shifts remain present problems before 2039 robots.
do: Save one **lesson fee** in good months after food and mortgage clear.
Apply for an **open music-shop job** after 2036 if cafe pay falls and lessons cannot cover it.

S4.quote: I would rather skip the savings envelope than borrow for groceries.
fieldNote: His savings plan is **conditional** on paid lessons after essential bills clear.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because recording tracks and the cafe fee could go before a school class is ready. A written cafe decision, supervised paid school block and an open shop post would give us options.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask the cafe owner whether a playlist buys groceries for a family. My children hear how much we need the cafe fee when I count our paid Sundays.

headlineQuote: My children hear how much we need the cafe fee when I count our paid Sundays.
portrait: At **43**, Tomas is a junior bassist with secondary school education, two children, a mortgage and less than one month saved.
His partner’s **care shifts** and cafe fees vary, leaving the household anxious even in AI Plateau.
He uses **AI occasionally** for practice sheets but checks fingerings and seeks supervised paid group teaching.
Across faster AGI dates, he seeks **written cafe dates**, lender help and a real music-shop opening if work falls.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could end recording income and the cafe fee before a supervised school class starts.
whatWouldHelp: A **written cafe decision**, paid school block and open music-shop post would give the family options.
